stages.stranger: Álvaro, from Colombia. I kept bees at home and I keep the swarms off the climbers here. Stand still if something lands on you, that's the whole trick.
stages.acquaintance: My uncle had a farm in the hills above Cartagena, coffee and plantains and eighty hives along the fence. I worked those hives for twenty years. My wife sold the honey off the back of a pickup on the coast road, and she sold it better than I ever kept it.
stages.companion: My wife is Marisela. She laughs at me for talking to the bees, and then she asks what I told them. When I came through, I was standing in the hives at dawn with the smoker in my hand. I think about whether she found the smoker on the ground, and what she thought.
stages.friend: My uncle died the week before I came through, and I never told the bees. My grandfather said if you don't tell them the news they leave, and I've been afraid ever since that I left them without a word. There's a hive of gentle sap-bees on this island, and the big wasps are tearing it apart. I want to save it. Will you help me hold them off?
stages.sworn: We saved them, all of them, and the queen is laying again. I took the first comb of honey on this world out of that hive this morning, and it tastes of the tree. Then I sat with the bees and told them everything: my uncle, Marisela, the farm and the pickup, and they listened to all of it. I feel lighter than I've felt in three years.

moments.prompt: He's asked you to help him save the sap-bees' hive.

options.text: We'll save them, and then you can tell them your news.
options.reply: Gracias, my friend. Walk slowly when we get close, they can feel your heart.
Only bees, yes. My grandfather would have stopped speaking to you for that.

moments.prompt: After the wipe he's sitting very still while everyone else is panicking.
moments.line: Breathe slowly, all of you. Panic is louder than blood, and everything out here can hear it.

options.reply: Good, that's better. Now we think, and then we go again.

options.text: Easy for you, nothing ever stings you.
options.reply: Everything stings me, friend. I just don't run from it.

lines.bored_warning: We've been standing still a long while, and even I get restless eventually. Let's find something to do.
lines.leaving_good: Good work, all of you, very good. I'm going back to Rootwater to see how the swarms are behaving.
lines.leaving_bored: It's too quiet out here, and the reeds at Rootwater need me. I'm going home for a while.
lines.after_wipe: Slowly, everyone, slowly. Stand up when your heart stops racing, not before.
lines.wipe_warning: I can take the stings, but the party can't take many more of these. We try once more, then we rest.
lines.wipe_leave: Enough for now. You'll find me on Rootwater Isle, out in the reeds.
lines.zone_warning: These things are too big for us, friend. Even a beekeeper knows when to close the hive.
lines.zone_leave: Too much danger here for this party. I'm going back to Rootwater.
lines.gear_refuse: No, no, I've only just got that one comfortable.
lines.gear_taken: Of course, take it. I wore a cotton shirt in eighty hives for twenty years.
lines.gear_short: If something heavy turns up, I'd wear it. The wasps here have opinions about my arms.
lines.gear_upgrade: Ah, that's beautiful work, and I thank you for it.
lines.back: Hola again, friend. The swarms are quiet on Rootwater and I'm free, so tell me where we're going.
lines.send_word: Álvaro has sent word from Rootwater Isle. The swarms are quiet and he's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: I left without a proper goodbye, and I'm sorry for it. Sit with me a minute and I'll explain.
lines.neglect: Ah, you came back! I'd started telling the bees you were lost.
lines.asked_to_stay: Bueno, one more. Then I go and check the reeds.
lines.on_break: Álvaro is back on Rootwater Isle, out in the reeds. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.
lines.mail_yes: Your letter found me in the reeds. I'll come to {town} and look for you at the inn, and I'll bring something sweet.
lines.mail_later: The swarms are restless this week, and the climbers need me close. I'll come when they settle.
lines.mail_see_me: This needs a proper talk, slowly, not ink. Come out to Rootwater and sit in the reeds with me.

town_arrive.text: Somebody here keeps bees. You can smell the wax on the wind if you're patient.
Let's find something to eat before we find anything to fight.

dungeon_clear.text: All done, and nobody ran. That's how it's supposed to go.

boss_down.text: Big, loud and in a hurry, that one. They never last.

close_call.text: Don't swat at it, stand still, let it pass.

zone_arrive.text: Listen to that hum in the grass. There are bees here, or something like them.
